items.title: Nehammer Denies Media Pressure
items.gist: A former chancellor faced questions in a parliamentary inquiry. His account is contested, and the committee is also examining a recording linked to the case.
items.summary: Former chancellor Karl Nehammer testified before a parliamentary inquiry into the Pilnacek case. The inquiry is examining claims that politicians tried to influence media coverage. Nehammer denied contacting ORF or the newspaper Kronen Zeitung to intervene. He said he spoke with the newspaper’s editor only after a witness raised the claim. The inquiry is also looking at a recording in which the late official Christian Pilnacek spoke of alleged political pressure. The parties in parliament disagree about the meaning of the evidence.
items.host_open: This inquiry has more twists than a courtroom drama, minus the popcorn. How does Nehammer’s testimony look to you?

items.title: Universities Seek More Funding
items.gist: Staff at Austria’s public universities want the government to reopen budget talks. They warn that the current plan may put teaching and research under pressure.
items.summary: Staff at Austria’s 22 public universities have asked the government to renegotiate their budget for 2028 to 2030. They say the planned funding does not cover the universities’ needs. The government has agreed on about 16 billion euros for the period. The universities’ umbrella body says about 18 billion euros would be needed just to cover inflation. University leaders have warned that major staff cuts may follow. The staff representatives say teaching or research could suffer if the budget stays as planned.
items.host_open: University budgets are not exactly light reading, but they shape campus life. Do you think the planned funding is enough?

items.title: Donations Lose Buying Power
items.gist: People in Austria gave more than a billion euros to charities last year. Inflation means those donations may support less work than before.
items.summary: A report says people in Austria donated 1.08 billion euros in 2025. The Fundraising Association Austria says rising prices have reduced charities’ purchasing power. Its director estimates that organisations have lost about a quarter of their financial impact since 2023. Private donations make up most of the sector’s funding, the report says. Older people were more likely to donate than younger adults. Social and health services received the largest share of donations.
items.host_open: A billion euros sounds enormous until inflation takes a bite. Did the report’s figures surprise you?

items.title: Snow Disrupts Austrian Travel
items.gist: Heavy snow caused crashes, delays and road closures across Austria. The A21 near Vienna was shut in both directions as conditions worsened.
items.summary: Heavy snowfall affected many parts of Austria on Thursday. The A21 motorway was closed in both directions between Steinhäusl and Vösendorf after vehicles became stuck. Traffic jams were reported in Vienna, and some local train services were delayed. Police, firefighters and road crews responded to crashes and other incidents. Forecasters warned that more snow was expected in several areas. Authorities urged drivers to slow down and allow extra travel time.
items.host_open: Austria got a sudden white blanket, and the roads got the hard part. How is the weather looking where you are?

items.title: Israeli Strikes Kill Eight In Gaza
items.gist: Health officials in Gaza reported eight deaths in overnight Israeli strikes. Israel said one strike targeted a Hamas figure; the military’s account of another was not immediately clear.
items.summary: Health officials said Israeli strikes killed eight Palestinians in Gaza overnight. The reported deaths were in Gaza City and Deir al-Balah. Officials said a man and his wife died when a residential apartment was hit. Israeli leaders said the military killed Khaled Abu Nada, a Hamas official responsible for economic and education affairs. The Israeli military said one strike targeted three militants, but did not immediately comment on another. The strikes came despite a ceasefire agreement reached more than a year ago.
items.host_open: More deaths have been reported despite the ceasefire, a painful reminder of how fragile it is. How are you feeling about the latest news?

items.title: EU Debates New Ukraine Loan
items.gist: EU leaders are discussing a proposed 45-billion-euro loan for Ukraine. They are also divided over the bloc’s long-term budget and how to share the costs.
items.summary: EU leaders met in Brussels to discuss a new loan for Ukraine and the bloc’s next long-term budget. The proposed loan is worth 45 billion euros. The European Commission’s plan would direct money to Ukraine’s economy and armed forces. Some governments oppose using EU funds for military support, while others argue that helping Ukraine is important for European security. The wider budget talks also reveal disagreements over farming, regional support and new spending priorities. Leaders may need more time before they reach a deal.
items.host_open: The EU’s budget table is crowded with competing priorities. Which issue do you think leaders will find hardest to agree on?

items.title: Norway Checks Religious Memberships
items.gist: Norway plans to send millions of text messages asking people to check their religious registration. The move follows reports that some people were listed without their knowledge.
items.summary: Norway plans to send text messages to people registered as members of religious groups. The messages will begin next week and go to residents aged 15 and over. People will be able to check their membership through a link. The government says the checks should help prevent public grants being paid for incorrect registrations. Reports have described complaints from people who say they never joined the groups. Registered faith and outlook communities can receive state funding based on their membership numbers.
items.host_open: A text message asking about religion is an unusual inbox arrival. Would you find that surprising?

items.title: Global Stocks Rebound
items.gist: European and Asian markets rose as investors bought technology shares. Caution about AI stocks and possible US tariffs remains in the background.
items.summary: Stock markets in Europe and Asia rose on Thursday. US markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday. Buying of shares linked to artificial intelligence helped lift some Asian markets. Investors are still cautious about AI companies and are watching proposed US tariffs on several trading partners. Germany’s DAX and France’s CAC 40 both climbed in early trading. Oil prices also rose amid continuing tensions in the Middle East.
items.host_open: Markets found some lift while investors kept an eye on the risks. Did the rebound surprise you?

items.title: Smart Glasses Assist Surgeons
items.gist: A hospital in Leipzig is testing a headset that overlays 3D anatomy with surgical information. Doctors say it can show important structures with great precision.
items.summary: Surgeons at a university hospital in Leipzig are using Apple’s Vision Pro headset in research. The device overlays three-dimensional images of a patient’s anatomy with information used during an operation. It can help show important structures during procedures, including surgery around the eye socket. The hospital has used the technology in about 30 operations so far. The report says the application remains limited to research in Europe. The technology aims to support surgeons, not replace their medical judgement.
items.host_open: A computer display in your field of vision is moving from science fiction to the operating room. Would that make you feel more confident or more cautious?

items.title: A Bookshop Gives Away 10,000 Books
items.gist: A bookseller in Bologna put thousands of books outside for people to take. He wanted to save them from being thrown away during a move.
items.summary: Bookseller Davide Scilabra offered nearly 10,000 books for free in Bologna. The books came from subjects including art, languages, philosophy and mathematics. He was moving his shop to a smaller, cheaper space. At first, he tried selling the books cheaply, but said many were taken without payment. He then decided to give the books away. The shop owner said they were still useful, and almost all had gone by the time of the report.
items.host_open: Ten thousand books on the pavement sounds like a book lover’s dream. Which shelf would you head for first?

items.title: James Sets NBA Triple-Double Record
items.gist: LeBron James became the oldest player in NBA history to record a triple-double. He did it in Philadelphia’s win over Miami.
items.summary: LeBron James recorded a triple-double in the Philadelphia 76ers’ 111–104 win over the Miami Heat. He scored 25 points, took 10 rebounds and made 12 assists. At nearly 42, he became the oldest player in NBA history to achieve the mark. The 76ers were leading the Eastern Conference with 15 wins from 19 games, according to the report. In another game, Kevin Durant passed 33,000 career points. The record highlights how long top players can remain productive in the league.
items.host_open: At nearly 42, James is still filling every column on the stat sheet. Did that record surprise you?
